figures.caption: Figure 3: TE decision plane at 4B scale. Each of 24 benchmarks is placed at its (VCR(x), ISR(x)) coordinates and coloured by the oracle preference. The dashed curve is the TE(x) = τ contour, a hyperbola because TE(x) = ISR(x) · VCR(x). The two shaded regions are the select-visual and select-text assignments of the rule TE(x) ≥ τ , and decision errors are marked with an ×. For oracle labeling, the visual arm is the better of VLM and VLM+Fov, matching the upper-bound definition in Tab. 2. The single scalar τ is fixed across all benchmarks. The rule is correct on 17/24 datasets (70.8%) at Qwen3-4B, raises the macro-average score from 45.9 to 47.4 (+1.5 points, +3.3% relative), and uses 10.3% fewer average input tokens than the LLM-only baseline model.

Table 12: Per-family theory-data validation. Predicted regimes are derived from the dominant term of C(x) in Eq. 8. Pred. sign denotes the expected LLM/VLM gap direction. “+” means LLM wins, “−” means VLM is non-degraded or better, and “N/A” means no fixed prediction for the mixed regime. The ∆ columns report observed family-average gaps at Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-32B. Positive values mean LLM beats VLM. Family ∆ values are computed from full-precision LLM and VLM scores and rounded to two decimals for display. Recomputing ∆ from the 1dp scores in Tab. 13 can give values differing by up to 0.06 across the 18 cells of this table due to per-dataset rounding accumulation.

Figure 1: Left: the text-only baseline. Right: our VTC framework. Given x, we first compute labelfree probes (W,L,TRR,VCR, γ), combine them into the transport-efficiency score TE(x), and route the instance under the rule TE(x) ≥ τ (Sec. 3.2). If the visual path is selected, x is rendered to an image, encoded by the ViT push-forward map, and read by a VLM augmented with foveation that re-encodes high-Cq patches (Sec. 3.3). Across the 24-benchmark suite, the label-free rule matches the per-dataset oracle on 17/24 datasets (70.8%), raises the macro-average score from 45.9 to 47.4 (+1.5 points, +3.3% relative), and uses 10.3% fewer average input tokens than pure-LLM.

Figure 2: The label-free proxy C(x) tracks the labelled operational gap ∆(x) on 24 NLP benchmarks with the Qwen3-4B backbone (LLM and VLM). (a) Mean ∆(x) = stext − svis within each C(x) tertile, with 8 datasets per bin and error bars of ±1 standard error. ∆ is reported in the native task metric, all on the same 0 to 100 scale. The mean ∆ increases monotonically from −6.9 in the low-C tertile to +10.1 in the high-C tertile, showing that the label-free proxy orders the C(x) tertiles consistently with the labelled operational gap. (b) Per-dataset decomposition of C(x) into its intra-patch component ∆intra(x) = α ·W (x) (Orange) and inter-patch component ∆inter(x) = β · L(x) (1− TRR(x)) (Green), matching Eq. 8. The composition varies systematically with task structure. ∆inter is largest on long-document summarization such as CNN/DM [15], XSum [32], GovReport [17], and BillSum [20], and on several high-coverage reasoning or classification inputs such as LogiQA [25] and BoolQ [10]. ∆intra remains substantial on precision-sensitive tasks such as QuALITY [34], RACE-H [21], ContractNLI [19], and IMDB [30]. This empirical separation is consistent with the factorization T# = Tinter ◦ Tintra in Eq. 6.
